When the top route still passes cameras, tries a point just off the road at each camera and routes through it, the way you would by long-pressing the map. Counts the license-plate reader (Flock) cameras on each route (a camera aimed across the road is left out, since it reads cross traffic) and auto-picks a lower-camera one when it costs only a little longer. Vela talks to Google\'s public endpoints straight from this device: no backend, no account, no API key. Google sees your IP, query and map area, not who you are.
House numbers come from OpenStreetMap and, in the US, OpenAddresses. A building that has no number in either shows none, even though search still finds the address through Google.

Vela\'s icons, plus anything extra Google has once you stop panning.
Searching, or tapping a place, still asks Google for hours, reviews and photos whichever you pick.

Tapping a place fetches its hours, reviews and photos from Google, and Vela remembers the match so the next tap is instant. Off = a tapped place shows only what Vela\'s data has (name, type, address, phone, website) and nothing about the tap reaches Google. Search and directions still use Google.
Where Vela\'s place data comes from

Vela's place data is Overture Maps, an open dataset of businesses maintained by Meta, Microsoft and others, plus AllThePlaces, which collects chains from their own store locators, with OpenStreetMap correcting where each shop actually sits. Vela bakes the three into map tiles and serves them from its own GitHub repository, so nothing about where you look goes to Meta or Google.

It streams in as you browse and downloads with a region for offline use. Where Vela has no data for an area yet, the map falls back to Google.

Search, place details, hours, reviews and photos always come from Google, whichever option you pick.
The non-business tier of place icons. Off shows businesses only.
Bus and rail stop icons at street zoom.
Small suits low-resolution screens like car head units, where the default icons render oversized.

Every couple of minutes during a drive, Vela asks Google for fresh traffic from your current position. That powers faster-route offers and the live arrival time, but it also tells Google where along the route you are. Off: your route still recalculates when you leave it.

Count cleared. Saved places, lists and trips are untouched.

Google\'s pages report on themselves: logging pings and the account bar\'s background calls. Nothing Vela shows needs them. They go out by default because a browser that never sends them looks less like a person to Google, and that is part of what decides whether your session gets the limited view. Turn this on to answer them on the phone instead.

Right now Google is giving this phone a limited view: fewer photos per page, no popular times on some places, and More reviews loads nothing. It usually lifts on its own after a while. A brand-new session starts out limited too, so starting one rarely helps.
Google is showing a limited view right now, so popular times and more reviews may be missing here.

Google remembers this phone by a cookie, so what Vela looks up while it lasts can be linked together, without any name or account. Starting a new one caps that. A new session gets a shorter view from Google for a while (fewer reviews, popular times missing on some places).
Start a new one every week (recommended)
Start a new one every day
Start a new one every time Vela opens (most private)

What this costs: Google treats every session as a new visitor, so you mostly get its shorter view (about five reviews, popular times often missing). Places load a little slower and use more data, because a new session\'s first answers come back trimmed and are asked again. Android restarts apps in the background, so this can mean several new sessions a day, and many new visitors from one connection can draw more of Google\'s bot checks. Google still sees your IP address, which links sessions from one connection over a short time anyway.
Recent searches, recent places, parking history and recorded trips. Saved places and lists stay.
Recent searches, recent places, parking history and every recorded trip will be deleted. This cannot be undone. Saved places and lists are not affected.
Saved places, lists, Home and Work, settings and downloaded regions are deleted from their own screens, never from here.

Google\'s public servers answer searches, place lookups, routes and the hidden pages. They see your IP address, the words you type, the map area or the route\'s endpoints, and Google\'s own logged-out session cookie. They never see a Google account, a name or an API key that marks the traffic as Vela\'s.

Saved places, lists, Home and Work, recent searches, parking history, settings and downloaded regions are stored only here. Vela has no server, no analytics and no crash reporting, and nothing on this screen is uploaded.

Vela cannot make Google forget a request it has already answered, and it cannot hide your IP address. Use a VPN or Tor for that. The session cookie is what links lookups while a session lasts; the weekly rotation caps it but does not erase the past. Google may also give a new session a limited view: fewer photos per page, popular times missing, and More reviews loading nothing.

Vela\'s own requests do not go to Google, with two exceptions you control: one cookieless shortener request when you open a shared short link, and the tiles of Google\'s traffic or satellite overlays if you turn those on. You lose reviews, photos, Google\'s opening hours, live arrival times, Street View and the satellite close-ups. Transit directions come from the open planner. Downloaded regions still work fully offline.

Nothing is sent to Google. Search uses OpenStreetMap and your downloaded regions, places on the map come from Vela\'s own data, and routes come from the open router with no live traffic. You lose reviews, photos, Google\'s opening hours, live arrival times, Street View and the satellite close-ups. Transit directions come from the open planner. Downloaded regions still work fully offline.
Off by default. When on, Vela keeps a short local log you can export and hand to a developer. Nothing is uploaded, and turning it off wipes the log.

Vela will record the GPS trace of each navigation on this phone, so a drive can be replayed for testing without driving it again. This is more revealing than diagnostics (it captures your exact routes) but it stays on the phone and is never uploaded. Turn it off any time.

Vela is a degoogled maps client: open tiles for the basemap, scraped Google for places, routing and traffic-aware ETAs, and a Piper voice that runs on the phone. GPLv3. No Play Services required.
Vela is free and ad-free. If it\'s become useful, a donation helps keep development going. Entirely optional.

Vela is OpenFreeMap\'s Liberty style with Vela\'s own colors, icons and road widths. The others are OpenFreeMap\'s Bright, Positron, Fiord and Black (its Dark style) as they come; Fiord and Black are dark whatever the theme.

Modern matches the Google app\'s current palette. Classic is Vela\'s earlier look: white roads, yellow motorways, true greens. Contrast is a night map with warm streets on slate land, for a glance from a mount; by day it draws as Modern.

The map, its streets, labels and house numbers are OpenStreetMap data, available under the Open Database License, served as vector tiles by OpenFreeMap. The businesses on the map in covered regions are places data from the Overture Maps Foundation (sourced from Meta and Microsoft), available under the Community Data License Agreement, Permissive 2.0. Place details, reviews, routing and traffic come from Google. Satellite imagery is from Esri and Google. How the voice says some 3,500 place names comes from English Wikipedia and its contributors, under CC BY-SA 4.0.
UK fuel prices come from the UK government\'s Fuel Finder, republished by matthewgall/fuelfinder-archive on GitHub. Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
